memoryReview.lesson: Do not copy an overhead pixel board, framed stage or conventional d-pad; the apartment must be experienced from fragile eye-height perspective.
Avoid a giant aggressive FPS action console; the old service revolver is a small tool inside a larger exploration and memory experience.

references.observation: A recognizable Soviet domestic flat emphasizes modest corridors, compact furnishings and characteristic older residential construction.
references.principle: Make lived-in Soviet housing feel personal and time-worn, not a generic violent horror stage.
references.application: Use glass-paneled lacquered doors, a living-room furniture wall, porcelain display, wall rugs and herringbone parquet.
references.avoid: Do not replace personal domestic specificity with a uniform industrial texture or fake neon highlights.

references.observation: The original HTML5 prototype changes chunks as a character's tile memory decays, but inconsistent game-map interfaces and partial merging create isolated rooms.
references.principle: Architecture rearranging itself behind the player is the central gameplay identity, not merely random corridors.
references.application: Use a bounded fully walkable apartment. Rewrite room door positions and furnishing only after leaving sight and physical vicinity.
references.avoid: Avoid partial merging of old remembered cells into new grids, which was able to strand walking paths.

references.observation: The Godot prototype already started experimenting with spatial movement, apartment cells, and projectile scripts.
references.principle: Player-scale spatial navigation fits the tension of a horror labyrinth better than reading square tiles from above.
references.application: Reuse the native first-person movement/shooting intent, but make fresh keyboard and touch input independent from mouse pointer lock.
references.avoid: Do not carry over engine-specific scene dependencies or half-connected controllers from the abandoned prototype.

references.observation: Existing Gloamstep demonstrates a fully localized mobile dungeon, objective counters and a deliberate exit route.
references.principle: On a small screen, important progress and escape should be visible without permanent panels or scrolling.
references.application: Show the real interior, its own wallpaper and worn wood; use a restrained objective line instead of a wide status control ribbon.
references.avoid: Avoid copying overhead tile rendering, the framing strips or a full directional control pad.

concepts.medium: Offline authored WebGL1 indoor 3D geometry, GLSL procedural surface patterns, rounded silhouettes and an independent first-person revolver model.
concepts.composition: Furnished apartment fills the whole screen, while small location, self-control, ammo and chapter progress marks hug the screen perimeter.
concepts.interaction: Pressing WASD or a left thumb translates freely in two axes; right drag changes gaze; E, shoot, reload and inventory directly change game state.
concepts.motion: Immediate camera parallax with minor walking bob, proportional furniture and silhouette movement, restrained firearm flash and animated memory instability.
concepts.rationale: A genuine inhabited flat makes forgotten domestic routes emotionally meaningful rather than another anonymous maze. All materials are generated locally.

concepts.medium: High-resolution 2D canvas and charcoal ink corridors rendered as an architectural memory diagram.
concepts.composition: Top-down floor plan drawn onto a stationary document with side navigation and a map scanner.
concepts.interaction: The player drags a cursor on the blueprint, while ink erases and redraws areas outside a radial sight cone.
concepts.motion: Ink wash evaporates in slow paper-grain transitions, leaving scratches before returning to the document.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because the old 2D presentation already obscured personal vulnerability and the sense of scale.

concepts.medium: CSS perspective projections of a paper diorama with separately articulated cardboard walls and doors.
concepts.composition: A central miniature room suspended between vertically arranged navigation documents and object descriptions.
concepts.interaction: Players physically rotate a cardboard room, then choose doors by tapping miniature handles one room at a time.
concepts.motion: Cardboard walls fold on hinges with a spring settling and paper-slot transition to the next isolated scene.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because one-room-at-a-time jumps weaken continuous navigation and make the world feel like a puzzle box.

selection.reason: The full-depth apartment best expresses unreliable recollection; persistent doors, the personal inventory and visually legible objects form one usable survival scenario.

rejected.reason: A legible overhead plan would be a clearer editor, but loses the horror of not seeing behind the player.
Hand-built CSS cardboard cannot affordably stream the corridors and continuous depth this mechanic depends on.

tools.reason: WebGL context, shaders, vertex buffers and geometric occlusion are implemented directly in renderer.mjs.
A custom vector double-portal emblem was authored for the launcher icon with a clear at-a-glance silhouette.
Native Node test runner can exercise connected portals and navigation across seeds without a browser.

assets.role: Aged half-open wooden apartment door with brass peephole and a suggestion of a faceless shadow, visible in the PocketWorks library.
assets.acceptance: Door silhouette, handle and peephole remain distinct in the 64-to-256-pixel icon range without text or neon glows.
assets.integration: Manifest, HTML tab icon and service-worker offline precache share the same authored SVG at icons/icon.svg.
assets.provenance: Custom original vector geometry created for NOT DEAD YET and based on ordinary domestic architecture rather than another game design.

assets.role: Real wall, floor, ceiling, furniture and object meshes colored by wood grain, aged plaster, patterned wallpaper, tile, cloth, enamel and brass GLSL materials.
assets.acceptance: Every room has recognisable furniture and a repeatable coherent material, and picking a memory object removes its visible 3D prop.
assets.integration: Renderer reads room data, dynamic item states and object coordinates from the chapter world; materials are compiled in its original local WebGL shader.
assets.provenance: Materials are mathematically authored original procedural shader patterns; no downloaded textures, fonts or online runtime resources.

assets.role: Polished wall-unit furniture, portrait glass doors with hinged leaves, wall carpets, enamel tea sets and geometry-based cast floor shadows.
assets.acceptance: Visual props sit on the actual apartment floor/walls and doors align with their physics collision polygons.
assets.integration: The renderer reads world.doors() directly, while world.canStand() uses the same shared panels geometry in doors.mjs.
assets.provenance: All geometry, sounds, textures and UI states are custom authored local source; no external app runtime assets.

assets.role: Asymmetric rooms and four subdued diegetic memory errors that change from player recognition.
assets.acceptance: Every room trace is physically reachable, visible only after offscreen mutation, clears on recognition, survives reload, cannot be farmed repeatedly.
assets.integration: Memory state and phase are serialized by Apartment.save(); game action and renderer read the same state.
assets.provenance: Original local procedural geometry; no external assets.

assets.role: Diegetic period-specific Bakelite radio with amber/ivory dial, wooden veneer and tactile tuning controls.
assets.acceptance: Positioned on the actual living-room table and the world-interaction radius matches the prop; mobile and desktop can reach all three channels.
assets.integration: The mesh reads Apartment.radio.channel; gameplay and offline WebAudio use the same state. Story text remains captioned and accessible when muted.
assets.provenance: Original procedural WebGL geometry, original local synthesized audio and Russian authored text, no downloaded assets.

evidence.firstFrame: An aged apartment door fills the main menu aside from the compressed title and one clear start action.
evidence.action: The menu closes into the furnished hall; left analog stick or keyboard traverses rooms while the right side looks around.
evidence.settled: A collected memory item disappears, its name fills one inventory entry and the door unlocks after all four items are found.

risks: Blocked keyboard motion or a dragging joystick returning zero must be caught by synthetic movement telemetry and real browser walkthrough.
Door mutation cannot seal a room or cover a user, quest prop or imagined pursuer; 300 seeded layouts should always be traversable.
Low-end WebKit shader compilation may fail with too many procedural operations; QA must inspect real frame output.
Tall portrait phone must show the interact, fire, reload and pause controls without preventing camera gestures.
comparisons: The earlier teal concrete chamber is replaced by warm aged domestic wallpaper, parquet, a bed, a kitchen and an old front door.
GLOAMSTEP remains a top-down grid crawler while this chapter has a free moving full-height first-person eye camera.
MELT//CRYPT focuses on combat and fantastical spaces rather than personal memory objects and subjective domestic exploration.
